correctness.rationale: The two fibre maps are strictly increasing homeomorphisms of one fixed interval and have only the common endpoint zeros of their displacement. Bounded (sub/super)martingale convergence forces endpoint limits. A reciprocal-endpoint drift identity plus SLLN excludes the unfavorable endpoint for nonzero bias and proves the coefficient c=π²/5 and the exact 1/n clock; summable O(1/n) reciprocal errors yield O(log n), permitting the standard Bernoulli CLT. A countable rational squeeze makes biased results simultaneous. In the fair case exact expectation conservation gives a linear endpoint-hitting law and an ordered rational cut yields one measurable uniformly distributed separator. Projection of every orbit to the common circle fixed point proves uniqueness of the annealed stationary probability. Exact symbolic identities and finite numerical diagnostics reproduce the local coefficients, but are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The source exhibits an unusual combination of a shared fixed circle point and a noninteger rotation number but does not explain the forward orbit geometry. The proposed result identifies an exact bias phase transition, a random uniform separator at balance, a sharp subexponential n^{-1} attraction clock, an explicit Gaussian fluctuation law and the sole annealed stationary circle state. These quantitative and sample-wise descriptions distinguish parabolic attraction from the exponential synchronization settings and provide a natural benchmark for random-neutral-point theory; they are not arbitrary parameter slices or numerical table entries.
